task: Change the secrets-indexing scan for DEC-853 (a time limit that grows with size, a bounded pool, a clean result reused by its hash) until the new acceptance tests in `tests/acceptance/W2-50/test_w2_50_secrets_scan_scale.py` pass, without breaking anything that passes today.

status: DONE. All 23 cases of the new acceptance file pass, the other 613 cases of the W2-50 suite still pass, and the work is committed as `a403309e`.

work_completed:
- Step 0, the sandbox check, passed. (a) Writing `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-kl5e` failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, exit 1. (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` gave `1ae28402…` (exit 0) and `git update-index --refresh` exited 0.
- Identity was as expected: `GOV_ROLE=engineer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-kl5e`, top level `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-50`, branch `w2/W2-50`, head `878467c9` at the start.
- **The time limit:** each gitleaks run may take `60 + len(input) / 1_000_000` seconds, where the input is the newline, the content and, for UTF-16, the copy without zero bytes. A store is therefore decided whenever gitleaks reads at 1 MB/s or faster. The 160 MiB case gets 228 s a run.
  - I did not use chunking, so no secret can be lost at a chunk's edge.
  - The input is now built once with `b"".join` and shared by both rule sets. Before, it was copied once per rule set.
  - `indexable` and `path_holds_secret` share this helper, so they gain only the size-aware limit and lose no check.
- **The pool:** `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=os.cpu_count())`, down from the default of cpu+4 (24 on this 20-core machine). Gitleaks uses about one core a run (measured at 0.3 s of CPU a run), so this pool does not oversubscribe the machine.
  - Files are started largest first, so a large store is never queued behind hundreds of small ones.
  - Files of 64 MiB or more are read and scanned at most two at a time (`BoundedSemaphore(2)`), which keeps memory in reason.
  - Results are still returned in path order.
- **The key of a clean result:** the SHA-256 of the store file's bytes (the same bytes that are scanned), checked against a scanner fingerprint. The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the form number (1), the rule sets `_rules(root)` produces, and the SHA-256 of the gitleaks binary `PATH` finds.
  - A change of `.gitleaks.toml`, of the gitleaks binary or of the scan's form makes no earlier clean result count.
  - Only a store that every rule set scanned to its end with no finding is added. A finding returns before it can be recorded.
- **The record:** `.gov-runtime/secrets-clean.json` inside the project (gitignored). It holds `{form, scanner, clean: [hex digests], check}`, where `check` is the SHA-256 of the body.
  - It is trusted only if it parses, has exactly those keys, its `check` matches, its form and scanner match, and every digest is 64 lowercase hex characters. Otherwise it is trusted for nothing and every store is scanned in full.
  - It is written to a temporary file in the same folder, flushed to disk, then renamed over the old record in one step, so an interrupted run leaves the old record or the new one.
  - It is written only after every store was decided. A run that raises writes nothing, and a record that cannot be written is skipped, so the next run scans in full.
  - The record file is itself scanned like any store; nothing under `.gov-runtime/` is excluded.
- **The label:** one line on standard error for each reused store, for example `secrets-indexing: clean result reused, not scanned again: .gov-runtime/store.db sha256 <64-hex>`. It holds the path and digest only, never content. A store that was scanned prints nothing. `__main__.py` is unchanged.
- The link rule (DEC-728, DEC-743 §6.1 (i), DEC-751 item 2), the rules, the UTF-16 handling, what a store's content is, how gitleaks is called, and every imported name are unchanged. `_store_content` gained an optional argument for bytes already read.

discoveries:
- `gov retrieve` is stale. All three questions I asked ("secrets-indexing check gitleaks timeout pool", "DEC-595 secrets scan runtime measurement", "where are cache records of a check kept inside .gov-runtime") returned `FACET_UNAVAILABLE`, with lexical and semantic both stale. They did not help, so I read files by name.
- Guard read refusals met: 0.
- A gitleaks run costs about 0.3 s of CPU on one core, even for tiny input. That is why the pool stays at the processor count rather than lower: a first full scan of the main tree's 3,987 files is about 8,000 runs, roughly 120 s on 20 cores.
- On the main tree, `store.db` is 253 MB and `code.db` is now 86 MB (P-W2-49 recorded 210 MB).
- `gov check` treats non-JSON standard output with exit 0 as GREEN, and the label goes to standard error, so it cannot change a check's status.

risks:
- If `store.db` is rewritten by most `gov` commands, its hash changes and it is scanned in full most runs; the reuse then mainly saves the many stable small files. The size-aware limit still lets it finish: about 36 s a run at the quiet 21 MB/s.
- At the 1 MB/s floor, a SQLite store with zero bytes is scanned as roughly bytes plus rows plus the zero-free copy, about 600–750 MB for `store.db`. Two rule sets one after the other could then exceed the declaration's 900 s. Each gitleaks run is within its own limit, but the check as a whole could still time out, which is fail-closed (red), never green.
- The record's `check` digest catches damage, not forgery. Anyone who can write the project could plant a record that makes a store count as clean. That is the same trust as writing the stores themselves; there is no key.
- A store's hash is taken from the bytes scanned, but for SQLite the rows are read through a separate connection. A database changing between those two reads could record a clean result whose rows text came from the newer state. The window is narrow.
- A new file, `.gov-runtime/secrets-clean.json`, appears after each check run. Any tool that expects an exact set of files under `.gov-runtime/` would see it. None of the suites I ran did.

lessons:
- W1-16, W1-19 and one W1-27 case cannot run inside this engineer sandbox (read-only `/tmp`, no `ollama.com`). The lead should run them outside it.
- W1-26 and W1-30 take more than 10 minutes as a whole. Run them by file, or with `-n 4` to `-n 6`, since pytest-xdist is installed.
